payload.answer: No main work should be allowed. We should always work in branches and worktrees and worktree gets cleaned-up once merged.

options.description: plumb tracks which records each session captured or edited, so a session asks only about those, even though main's changes are shared. Small extra bookkeeping per session; a session never asks about another session's uncommitted edits in main.
options.label: Records it created or edited itself

options.description: Every session in main's checkout counts all of main's uncommitted changes as its work. No new bookkeeping, but two sessions in main may both ask you about the same records (answered once, it closes in both).
options.label: Everything uncommitted in main

options.description: A session without its own branch never asks; its questions wait in /plumb status. Simplest, but work done in main never prompts you, even on records it changes.
options.label: None: only branch sessions ask

payload.question: A session's "work" would be what its branch changes compared with main: the same records the merge check already looks at (your INT-102 rule). But several sessions can work directly in the main checkout with no branch of their own, sharing one set of uncommitted changes. For a session in main's checkout, which questions should it ask you?
